original_question: Fix a homological degree s and let Sq^0: Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) -> Ext_A^{s,2t}(F_2, F_2) be the squaring operation induced by the Frobenius map on the dual Steenrod algebra. If Im((Sq^0)^i) denotes the image of the i-fold iterate on Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2), does there exist a number r = r(s) such that for every i >= r the map (Sq^0)^{i-r}: Im((Sq^0)^r) -> Im((Sq^0)^i) is an isomorphism? Equivalently, for fixed s, is every finite Sq^0-family in Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) bounded in length by some r(s)?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Conjecture 2.1, "Sq^0 is eventually isomorphic on the Ext groups," with nearby Observation 2.2 and Theorem 2.3 providing the paper's immediate refinement and motivation. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target almost verbatim: it fixes the homological degree s, uses the Frobenius-induced operation Sq^0 on Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2), defines Im((Sq^0)^i) as the image of the i-fold iterate on Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2), asks for eventual isomorphism of the image tower for every i >= r, and gives the same equivalent reformulation in terms of finite Sq^0-families that the paper itself states immediately after the conjecture. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
missing_details: State explicitly that A is the mod 2 Steenrod algebra and A_* is its dual; the paper defines Sq^0 via the Frobenius map A_* -> A_*, x -> x^2. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Clarify that Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) means the full group in fixed homological degree s, i.e. across all internal degrees t, not a single bidegree Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2). ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

Define "finite Sq^0-family" in the paper's sense: a family under repeated Sq^0 in Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) having only finitely many nonzero terms; the paper phrases this as having at most r(s) nonzero elements. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

If you want the full nearby paper context, note that the sharper value r(s) = s - 2 is not part of the formal conjecture; it appears separately as Observation 2.2. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))

The local motivation should be recorded if context matters: Theorem 2.3 proves the analogous eventual-isomorphism statement, with bound s - 2, for Kameko's Sq^0 on the domain of the Singer transfer. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
refined_question: Let A be the mod 2 Steenrod algebra, let A_* denote its dual, and let Sq^0: Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2) -> Ext_A^{s,2t}(F_2, F_2) be the squaring operation induced on the cohomology of the Steenrod algebra by the Frobenius map A_* -> A_*, x -> x^2. For a fixed homological degree s, write Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) for the full Ext group in degree s over all internal degrees t, and let Im((Sq^0)^i) be the image of the i-fold iterate on Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2). Is it true that there exists a number r = r(s), depending only on s, such that for every i >= r the map (Sq^0)^{i-r}: Im((Sq^0)^r) -> Im((Sq^0)^i) is an isomorphism? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each fixed s, does every finite Sq^0-family in Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2) have at most r(s) nonzero elements? ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Hưng's Conjecture 2.1 in Section 2. The paper introduces exactly the same Sq^0 on Ext_A^{s,t}(F_2, F_2), states the eventual-isomorphism condition on the image tower Im((Sq^0)^i) inside Ext_A^s(F_2, F_2), and then immediately restates it as a bounded-length statement for finite Sq^0-families. Observation 2.2 supplies the guessed bound r(s) = s - 2, while Theorem 2.3 gives the corresponding eventual-isomorphism result for Kameko's Sq^0 on the domain of the Singer transfer, which is presented as the motivation for the conjecture. ([msp.org](https://msp.org/gtm/2007/11/gtm-2007-11-020s.pdf))
